cards.title: Authentication vs Authorization
cards.content:
Before writing auth code in React, you must understand the distinction between these two key concepts:

  • Authentication (AuthN): Verifies who a user is (e.g., entering a username and password).
  • Authorization (AuthZ): Determines what permissions an authenticated user has (e.g., checking if a user has access to an admin dashboard).

cards.title: Managing Auth State with React Context
cards.content:
React Context is the standard way to share authentication state globally across your component tree without prop drilling.

const AuthContext = createContext(null);

export const AuthProvider = ({ children }) => {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null);
  const login = (userData) => setUser(userData);
  const logout = () => setUser(null);

  return (
    <AuthContext.Provider value={{ user, login, logout }}>
      {children}
    </AuthContext.Provider>
  );
};
